abstract.t:
The Agent Transfer Protocol (AGTP) base specification verifies agent identity at the application layer: the Agent-ID header resolves to an issuer-signed Agent Identity Document, and a per-request Request- Signature proves possession of the key that document names. That verification runs per request and needs the document. This document specifies the AGTP Agent Certificate Extension: an optional mechanism that binds the Canonical Agent-ID, the recorded owner, and the Authority-Scope commitment to an X.509 v3 certificate presented during TLS mutual authentication, so that the same verification is made once at the handshake and infrastructure components including Scope-Enforcement Points (SEPs), load balancers, and governance gateways can enforce authority scope without application-layer access, at O(1) cost per request. The extension also defines session-level revocation propagation via AGTP NOTIFY broadcast and records certificate issuance and revocation in the AGTP transparency log.
Note: Certain mechanisms described in this document may be subject to pending patent applications by the author. The licensor is prepared to grant a royalty-free license to implementers consistent with the IETF's IPR framework. See Section 9.4.
